name: browserai-payload
description: The vendored @playwright/mcp payload. Never published; this file exists only so the payload build has something to resolve.
//: THIS IS THE FLOAT, NOT A PIN. `latest` is the npm dist-tag, re-resolved from
an empty node_modules on every payload build. package-lock.json beside this
file records what it resolved to and is a provenance stamp, never a target:
build/Build-Payload.ps1 deletes the lock before installing, so nothing here
playwright-core is deliberately NOT declared as a DEPENDENCY here. It arrives
as @playwright/mcp's own exact dependency, and upstream publishes daily alphas:
on 2026-08-15 npm `latest` for playwright-core was 1.62.1 while the version
that actually ships was 1.63.0-alpha-2026-08-05. Declaring it would create a
second, independently floating source for a version upstream pins exactly.
See CLAUDE.md, 'Versioning: everything floats, the build freezes it'.
//overrides: A DATED EXCEPTION WITH A WRITTEN EXIT, taken 2026-09-17 by the maintainer
(Q210 = a). It is NOT a pin around an absence and it is NOT a precedent; see
DECISIONS.md, 'The two exceptions to the versioning policy'.
the `filePaths` config key and PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_FILE_PATHS is
project's own ask, microsoft/playwright#42497). This override pulls that one
build forward underneath the wrapper rather than waiting for the wrapper to
THE EXIT, and it is mechanised rather than remembered: this entry is DELETED
the day @playwright/mcp `latest` pins a playwright-core at or above
goes red on that day, naming this key and this file, and build/Build-Payload.ps1
refuses the build with the same instruction.
NOTHING ELSE MAY BE ADDED HERE ON THIS PRECEDENT. The argument is a merged
upstream fix that one wrapper release has not caught up with, which is a
condition that expires; it is not a preference, a workaround for a break, or
a way to hold a version back.
